minutes.headline: Assessors agreed to release the website as is, and asked staff to analyze excess overlay for the town manager.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors met in person only, with no Zoom or live feed. They welcomed a new part-time data collector and heard the assessor's monthly report, including MUNIS problems and new-growth inspections. They discussed an overlay analysis requested by the town manager and argued over releasing the website and the financial policies document. They prioritized the 41A, 41C/D and 17F exemption work for the fall town meeting warrant and approved withdrawing a parcel from Chapter 61B.

votes.motion: Accept the June 29th (as heard) minutes as amended.
Allow withdrawal of a property from Chapter 61B.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager formally asked the board to evaluate what excess overlay is available. The board discussed averaging several years of abatements excluding an anomalous year and presenting a recommendation.
Outstanding personal property taxes would come out of overlay and the tax collector's figures are needed. Motor vehicle abatements do not come out of overlay.

budget_items.topic: FY2024 supplemental bills for new construction
budget_items.what_was_said: Five supplemental bills for new construction were sent out, approved at the last meeting.
An invoice for the contractor's yearly appraisal of utilities was signed.
Business cards were purchased and dues to the Massachusetts Association of Assessing Officers were approved for signature.
A large volume of motor vehicle excise abatements was received in the past month.
A member proposed asking town meeting to reduce the 41A deferral interest rate from the state-set rate. Other towns charge lower rates.
Staff were looking for the state reimbursement amount for 41D but had found nothing yet.
The board asked how the town budgets for excise revenue. It was said the town accountant sets the estimate conservatively on the recap sheet.
The town is starting the budget process earlier than normal, and staff are getting vendor estimates.

decisions.decision: Assessor staff to put together an overlay analysis and recommendation for the board, targeted for next week.
The website will be released as is, with a table of contents/site map deferred to later; the chair declared it done.
Spelling errors found on the website may be pointed out to the webmaster and corrected.
A member will draft a 41A warrant article proposal, to be reviewed at the next meeting and sent to the town manager by the 17th.
A member will build a matrix on 41D, 17F and 41A, with 41D as the priority.
The next meeting is tentatively set for September 16th, with September 30th as a fallback.
Executive session minutes for the 29th to be emailed to the board if permitted, otherwise brought to the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors agreed to release its new website as is, deferring a site map or table of contents, after a dispute over whether to wait.
The town manager formally asked the board to evaluate how much excess overlay is available; staff were told to prepare an analysis and recommendation, targeted for next week.
Members were assigned work on 41A, 41C/D and 17F exemptions ahead of the fall town meeting warrant, including a draft 41A warrant article for the town manager.
The board voted to allow a property's withdrawal from Chapter 61B; the vote tally was not audible in the recording.
The board discussed feedback on the town's financial policies document and took no action; the next meeting is tentatively September 16.

why_it_matters: Excess overlay is money set aside for abatements that may be freed for other uses, so the analysis bears on how much the town has available when it sets the tax rate.

The 41A deferral and the 41C/D and 17F exemptions, which may come to the fall town meeting as warrant articles, are the kind of local-option changes residents are asked to vote on, and they affect what some older or eligible homeowners owe.
watch_next: The staff overlay analysis and recommendation, targeted for the following week, and the draft 41A warrant article due to the town manager by the 17th.
The next Board of Assessors meeting, tentatively September 16, with September 30 as the fallback.
